# pipigx frozen PHP product oracle

The reviewed `inputs.json` contains 42 synthetic metadata scenarios. It is not a production response fixture and it is not generated by Go.

`produce-pipigx.py` archives unchanged PHP commit `25beaee107f8c1a208ced9deb3c637068445e316` (tree `e4b9d40f5e6c12a86fff629c105553886b434dcd`) and requires PHP 8.3.6. The original platform functions execute against a strict cURL response tape, then the original entry JSON flags (480), adapter and public policy produce `php-baseline.json`. The manifest records the inputs, producers, immutable PHP source hashes, fixed clock and response digest. Unknown, reordered or unused requests fail generation.

The Go baseline tests use only that input tape and compare parser output, entry wire, request sequence, normal/debug public response, stable identities and defaults against the fixed PHP output. Successful tests export actual Go views through `DOKITOOL_GO_PIPIGX_OUTPUT`; they never write expectations. `internal/api/pipigx_http_test.go` also exercises the actual catalog and HTTP handler for every fixture and resolves each successful item plus an absent target.

The controlled executor still checks purpose, URL authorization, metadata byte limit, method, headers, body, redirect handling and deadlines. This proves offline contract behavior, not current platform accessibility or a real browser/file save.

The original float guard near PHP_INT_MAX precedes exact string-to-int conversion. Flags 480 apply JSON_NUMERIC_CHECK before adaptation. Invalid middle video URLs retain an item-index gap, non-array observations are filtered before indexing, and unsupported image fields never create an album. Go explicitly supplies libcurl implicit Accept and suppresses the Go default User-Agent; all other recorded request fields stay exact.

The fixed PHP observation for `wire/exponent-title` is authoritative: the string `1e3` becomes JSON number `1000`, and the adapter emits title `"1000"`. Its reviewed scenario description anticipated a float being omitted; that hypothesis was disproved by PHP. The frozen input/expected bytes are retained, and Go must match the observed result.
